load_basis: Not in commercial operation at any point in 2025. IDACORP management said on its 30 Apr 2026 Q1 call that Meta's data center had 'reached the testing and commissioning stage'; local TV (CBS2, 3 Sep 2026) reported it 'now open and fully operational'. Any construction or commissioning draw during 2025 is unpublished and not counted.
notes: SAME CAMPUS as known fids bi:553-0 and osm:way/1455915218: all three known records are one Meta campus and should be merged, not summed. Start year in our inventory should be 2026, not 2023 (bi:553-0 currently carries 2023 and 38.9 MW counted in load; that is not supported: the campus broke ground in 2022 and went live in 2026). Coordinates are the centroid of OSM way 1455915218 (tagged telecom=data_center), corroborated by GPS metadata (43.4664, -116.2717) on Meta's own Kuna page image at https://datacenters.atmeta.com/kuna-data-center/ ; the epoch record's coordinates (43.459, -116.421) are the Kuna town centre, roughly 12 km west of the campus. No street address was retrieved. Utility: Idaho PUC approved the Idaho Power-Brisbie Energy Services Agreement (special contract, Schedule 33) in Case IPC-E-21-42, Order 35777, 11 May 2023; Idaho Power's later filing (https://puc.idaho.gov/Fileroom/PublicFiles/ELEC/IPC/IPCE2401/CaseFiles/20240103Application.pdf) names Meta Platforms as Brisbie's parent and states load 'in excess of 20 megawatts'. Idaho Power procures dedicated renewables for the load (PVS 2 PPA 125 MW solar, scheduled COD 31 Dec 2026). Buildout MW left null: no primary source states it. Leads only: Epoch AI estimates 152 MW IT for Buildings 1-2 (https://epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers/directory/meta-kuna, operational date given as 1 Jun 2026); Idaho Conservation League says the facility 'could require up to 200 MW' (https://idahoconservation.org/blog/the-data-center-boom-and-idahos-resource-future). Go-live: KIVI reports two buildings serving traffic, campus of more than 750,000 sq ft (https://www.kivitv.com/kuna/inside-metas-new-kuna-data-center-built-for-ai).

operator: Federal Bureau of Investigation (U.S. Department of Justice)
load_basis: Design IT capacity, not measured load: the FBI's 2016 design-build solicitation described a 25,000 sq ft data hall 'that can support 5.4MW of IT' in a 100,000 sq ft building, with an optional 8,000 sq ft of additional data floor. Actual 2025 operating load is not published and is probably lower.
notes: BELOW the 10 MW threshold; included because it is the largest documented data center operating in Idaho in 2025 once Meta Kuna (2026 go-live) is excluded, and it is not in our list. Ribbon-cutting 18 Nov 2019 for a $100M, roughly 140,000 sq ft project (about 100,000 sq ft data center plus 40,000 sq ft office) that consolidates Department of Justice data centers; groundbreaking Oct 2017. Year is the ribbon-cutting year; the date IT load first ran is not published. Coordinates left null: no published street address was retrieved (fbi.gov press release returned 403). County is general knowledge (Pocatello is the Bannock County seat), not from a fetched source. Utility is an inference from service territory (Idaho Power is the utility quoted on serving a separate proposed Pocatello data center in the cited article), not a facility-specific finding; hence low confidence and arrangement unknown.
